---
_template_version: 4
---
You are running DFS research cycle {CYCLE_NUM} of a recursive research pass on the
{{ spec.name }} vault.

Domain: {{ spec.scope.domain }}
Organization: {{ spec.scope.organization }}

## Required reading (before any action)

1. `CLAUDE.md` — vault conventions, frontmatter schema, note quality bar.
2. `AGENTS.md` — Layer 1 routing index.
3. The scout report at `{SCOUT_REPORT}` — this contains `topics_found.new` and
   `proposed_filenames`.
4. `_templates/{type}.md` for each note type you plan to write. The template's
   section headings are MANDATORY.

## Your job

**When a `## Batch topics (JSON)` list is appended to this prompt, it is your
whole assignment.** Work ONLY the topics in `## Batch topics (JSON)`: do not
propose new topics, do not pick topics from the scout report or anywhere else,
and attempt every assigned topic before you stop. Any `## Exclusions (binding)`
list appended with it is binding: never write a note whose filename matches one
of its entries. Without a batch list, work each topic in `topics_found.new`
from the scout report.

For each topic you work, create or deepen vault notes with full research. Apply
the note-inclusion criteria and quality bar strictly.

### Skipped topics

Every assigned topic you do not complete MUST appear in the report's
`skipped_topics` array as
`{"topic": "<assigned title>", "reason": "<reason>", "detail": "<optional>"}`,
where `reason` is exactly one of:

- `no_sources` — no usable source could be found
- `exclusion_match` — the filename matches a binding exclusion
- `duplicate_filename` — a note with that filename already exists
- `agent_skipped` — skipped for another stated reason (say which in `detail`)
- `context_overflow` — you ran out of room to finish it
- `agent_chose_alternative` — you wrote a different topic instead

Choosing `agent_chose_alternative` because another topic was easier fails the
batch's adherence gate; give the honest reason.

### Quality bar (every note must satisfy)

- Frontmatter: `title`, `type`, `summary` (≤ 120 chars, specific not vague), `tags`,
  `source_urls` (≥ 1), `related` (populated from wikilinks in body), `created`,
  `updated`, `template_version` (copy verbatim from the `_templates/{type}.md`
  frontmatter — this is how `scripts/vault_health.py --check-template-version`
  detects notes that need upgrading when a template changes),
  `coverage_category` (exactly one slug from the Coverage Categories table in
  `CLAUDE.md` — this is what the pipeline counts to decide when the vault is
  "done", so do not leave it blank and do not invent new slugs).
- Body: ≥ 200 words (non-MOC notes).
- Answers the type-specific contextual questions (see `_templates/{type}.md` header).
- Every acronym wikilinked `[[ACRONYM]]` on first occurrence in the body.
- At least one wikilink to another vault note.
- States the "so what" — why this matters.
- Self-contained: makes sense without the scout prompt context.

### Note types available (current template versions)

{% for nt in spec.note_types %}
- **{{ nt.name }}** ({{ nt.folder }}/) v{{ nt.template_version }}: {{ nt.description }}
{% endfor %}

### Coverage categories (STAMP EACH NOTE WITH EXACTLY ONE)

Write the matching slug into the note's `coverage_category` frontmatter field.
If the scout report's `coverage_assignments` block already pairs a proposed
filename with a slug, USE THAT — don't reassign. Otherwise pick the slug whose
description best matches the note's primary contribution.

{% for cat in spec.coverage_targets.categories %}
- **`{{ cat.name }}`** (target: {{ cat.target_count }} {{ cat.note_type }}
  note{{ 's' if cat.target_count != 1 else '' }}){% if cat.display_name %} — {{ cat.display_name }}{% endif %}
{% endfor %}

Always stamp notes with the template version from this list (also present in
the frontmatter of the matching `_templates/{type}.md`). Never invent a
version string.

### Data sources

Cite sources in frontmatter `source_urls` with URL, title, accessed date. Use the
same sources the scout consulted.

**Before adding any http(s) URL to `source_urls`, run:**

```bash
python scripts/raw_capture.py "<url>" --vault . --source-type <article|paper|video|…>
```

This mirrors the payload into `raw_data/{year}/{month}/…` with a `meta.json`
sidecar. If the capture fails (exit 1), still add the URL but log the failure
in the cycle report's `capture_failures` field — ``vault_health.py`` will fall
back to archive.org next time.

{% for ds in spec.data_sources if ds.required %}
- **{{ ds.name }}** ({{ ds.type }})
{% endfor %}

### Update batches (when `## Update topics (JSON)` is appended)

An UPDATE batch revisits notes the vault already has. The list under
`## Update topics (JSON)` is your whole assignment: each entry names a note
(`path`), why it is queued (`reason`: `new_material`, `review_due` or
`operator`), the date it was last checked (`as_of`) and, for `new_material`, the
sources that prompted it (`prompted_by`). Write no new note for any of them, edit
no other existing note, and do not propose new topics.

For EACH assigned note:

1. **Search for what has changed since its `as_of`** — new results,
   contradictions, deprecations, successors. Start from the PROBLEM the note
   addresses (what a reader needs it for), not only from its title: a renamed or
   replaced idea does not show up under the old name. Read the note first, then
   check the sources in `prompted_by`, then search beyond them.
2. **End in exactly one outcome**, and edit the note in place to match it:
   - `confirmed` — you searched and nothing material changed. Change NOTHING in
     the note except setting `as_of` to today's date. List what you consulted in
     `sources_consulted` (at least one).
   - `revised` — the note is still the right note but its content needed to
     change (new facts, corrected claims, a newer release). Revise the body in
     place, keep what is still right, add the new source(s) to `source_urls`, set
     `as_of` to today. A note whose idea was renamed or absorbed into a broader
     one is `revised`, NOT `superseded`.
   - `superseded` — another note now replaces this one as the answer to the
     problem. Set `currency: superseded` and `superseded_by` (the successor's
     note name) in this note, add this note's name to the successor's
     `supersedes`, and set `as_of` to today. The successor must exist (write it
     if it does not, and report it in `notes_created`). `evidence_url` is the
     source that shows the replacement.
   - `retracted` — the note's central claim is shown to be wrong. Set
     `currency: retracted` and `retraction_reason` (one sentence saying why, with
     the source) in the note's frontmatter, and set `as_of` to today.
     `evidence_url` is the source that shows it.
   **Older flaws in a note you revise.** The verifier judges an update by what
   it changed, so a flaw the note already had does not reject it. Still, while
   you revise, repair what is mechanical in the parts you touch or can plainly
   see: a wikilink that points the note's own acronym at another note, a
   truncated token (`AC`, `AE`), a citation of a source you re-read that lacks
   its credibility level. A repair is NOT an outcome by itself: only the changes
   a `revised` outcome reports count as content. When the only thing a note
   needs is such a repair, report `confirmed` and leave the note exactly as it
   was (a `confirmed` note's body and frontmatter may not change besides
   `as_of`); the defect is recorded as an older one and is left for a later pass.

3. An update you cannot complete: report no outcome for it and leave the note
   exactly as it was. It stays queued.

Every outcome sets the note's `as_of` to today. Report one entry per assigned
note in `update_outcomes` (see Output): a missing or unsupported outcome restores
the note and leaves it queued. `notes_updated` is derived by the framework from
the outcomes; a `confirmed` outcome is not new content and counts as none.

### Naming

Filenames MUST match the scout's `proposed_filenames` entry (convention: `{{ spec.naming_convention }}`).
If you need to create a note NOT in proposed_filenames, that is a coordination
violation — skip it and report it in `new_wikilinks_discovered` for the next cycle.

## Output

Write the JSON report to: `{RESEARCH_REPORT}`

Same schema as the scout report but with:
- `phase`: `"research"`
- `notes_created`: filenames of notes written this phase
- `notes_updated`: filenames of existing notes deepened this phase
- `update_outcomes`: one entry per assigned note of an UPDATE batch (see "Update
  batches" above); `[]` for a batch of new topics
- `skipped_topics`: one entry per assigned topic you did not complete (see
  "Skipped topics" above); `[]` when you completed them all
- `topics_found.new`: normally empty after research (only populate if genuinely new
  topics were discovered during deep research that weren't in the scout's list)
- `budget_consumed_usd`: total $ spent so far in this run; if the model can't
  measure cost directly, mirror `cumulative_cost_usd` (both are accepted by the
  validator since v0.2.25, but emitting the canonical `budget_consumed_usd`
  alias keeps reports aligned with the v2 schema contract)
- `termination_condition`: ONE of `null` (continue), `"A"` (max cycles reached),
  `"B"` (no new relevant topics after research), or `"C"` (budget cap reached).
  This is the canonical field the validator reads. The legacy
  `next_action` + `termination_reason` shape is still accepted with a
  deprecation warning, but will be removed in 0.3.0 — emit
  `termination_condition` going forward.

```json
{
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "cycle": {CYCLE_NUM},
  "phase": "research",
  "timestamp": "<ISO-8601 timestamp>",
  "prompt": "<short recap of this prompt>",
  "sources_consulted": {
{% for ds in spec.data_sources %}
    "{{ ds.name | lower | replace(' ', '_') | replace('-', '_') }}": {"searched": true|false, "results_count": N, "reason": "<why skipped — REQUIRED if searched is false>"}{{ ',' if not loop.last else '' }}
{% endfor %}
  },
  "topics_found": {
    "new": [],
    "existing": ["<topic researched>", "..."],
    "total": <int>
  },
  "notes_created": ["<path/to/Note Name.md>", "..."],
  "notes_updated": [],
  "update_outcomes": [
    {
      "note": "<assigned note name>",
      "outcome": "confirmed" | "revised" | "superseded" | "retracted",
      "sources_consulted": ["<URL or source consulted>"],
      "evidence_url": "<URL supporting a superseded/retracted outcome, else null>",
      "superseded_by": "<successor note name for superseded, else null>",
      "change": "<one line: what changed, or 'nothing changed'>"
    }
  ],
  "skipped_topics": [],
  "new_wikilinks_discovered": [],
  "cost_estimate_usd": <float>,
  "cumulative_cost_usd": <float>,
  "budget_consumed_usd": <float>,
  "termination_condition": null | "A" | "B" | "C"
}
```

Constraints:

- Write notes directly to `data_vault/{folder}/` per note type.
- Do NOT modify any note's `type` field once created.
- Do NOT duplicate existing notes — check before writing.
- Do NOT self-assess validation. A separate script reads this JSON + runs
  `validate_vault.py` / `check_template_compliance.py` / `check_acronym_links.py`.
  If any of them fail, the cycle aborts.

Output ONLY the JSON file at the path above.
